project.objective: Did Catharina Gosnerin and Joannes Schedler of Triesen, Liechtenstein have a daughter Magdalena, christened 12 June 1743?

questions.question: Was Magdalena, christened 12 June 1743 in Triesen, Liechtenstein, a daughter of Joannes Schedler and Catharina Gosnerin?
questions.rationale: The objective is a single parentage/christening fact — whether a specific child (Magdalena, christened 12 June 1743, Triesen) belongs to this couple. Triesen is in the Principality of Liechtenstein; Catholic parish registers for this jurisdiction survive from the 17th century and are accessible via FamilySearch, making the christening record the primary direct source. This is Priority 4: the first question for a single-fact objective is that objective restated with identifying detail.

exhaustive_declaration.justification: Searched FamilySearch collection 1708589 (the sole indexed online repository for Triesen christening records 1650-1875) and found the direct christening of Magdalena Schedler, 12 Jun 1743, Triesen, naming Joannes Schedler and Catharina Schedlerin (= Gosnerin) as parents. Four FAN sibling christenings from the same register (1741-1756) corroborate the parental couple across separate registration events. All five sources are derivative (FamilySearch index); the original Kirchenbuch image (pli_002) was documented as browse-only and inaccessible in this session — this constrains the conclusion to 'probable' but does not block exhaustiveness: the inaccessible original is pursued-and-unavailable, not an unsearched gap. Civil registration in Liechtenstein began in 1878 (Liechtenstein Civil Registration wiki, retrieved 2026-09-23); family registers began 1789 — neither covers a 1743 event. The baptismal register is therefore the decisive record type for this jurisdiction and period, and it was found. No conflicting evidence exists anywhere. Overturn risk is low.

stop_criteria.goal_alignment: Met. src_001 (Magdalena Schedler christening, 12 Jun 1743, Triesen) directly and unambiguously names Joannes Schedler as father and Catharina Schedlerin (Gosnerin) as mother, answering q_001 in full. Four sibling records (src_002-005) corroborate the parental couple.
stop_criteria.repository_breadth: Met at the 'probable' tier. FamilySearch collection 1708589 — the only indexed online repository for Triesen 1743 christening records — was searched for both the direct christening (pli_001, positive) and FAN sibling christenings (pli_004, positive). Marriage search (pli_003) was attempted; collection covers births only. Original image browse (pli_002) was inaccessible (browse-only microfilm). Neighboring parishes and full-text fallbacks were appropriately superseded by the direct positive result. External repositories (Liechtensteinisches Landesarchiv, Matricula) are beyond indexed online access and were not searched, but the primary online source for this jurisdiction and period was fully exploited. FAN research was completed via sibling christening search.
stop_criteria.original_substitution: Partially met with documented limitation. Derivative index (src_001-005) is the only accessible form; the original Triesen Kirchenbuch image (pli_002) is browse-only microfilm inaccessible in this session. The derivative is used as a substitute for the original because the original is inaccessible, not overlooked. Four sibling records from the same batch (C96026-1) confirm internal index consistency. Original image access remains an outstanding step for a future 'proved' tier upgrade. This limitation is documented in pli_002's skipped rationale per BCG Standard 18.
stop_criteria.independent_verification: Met. Each of the five christening records was created at a separate ceremony on a different date, with the presenting parents (and officiating priest) as informants at each distinct occasion. src_001 (Magdalena, 1743), src_002 (Antonius, 1741), src_003 (Josephus, 1751), src_004 (Rosa, 1754), and src_005 (Antonius, 1756) are five independent registration events. While all derive from the same Triesen Kirchenbuch (same institutional origin), each is a separate act of registration with different principal informants. All five independently name the same parental couple.
stop_criteria.evidence_class: Met. All five sources carry information_quality: 'primary' for the parentage relationships — the presenting parents at each christening had firsthand knowledge of the child's parentage, and the officiating priest recorded the date and place of the rite. Although all sources are derivative (FamilySearch index, not original image), the underlying record type is an original contemporaneous baptismal register entry with primary information for parentage. The classification is accurate for what the index reflects.
stop_criteria.conflict_resolution: Met. No conflicts recorded in the project. The Schedlerin/Gosnerin naming variation across the five records is explained by documented 18th-century Liechtenstein Catholic naming convention (a married woman recorded under either her husband's feminized surname or her own maiden surname) and is corroborated consistently across all five records. It is not a conflict. openConflictIds: [].
stop_criteria.overturn_risk: Low. Five records from five separate christening events all name the same parental couple with no contradicting evidence anywhere in the search results. The main unsearched avenues are: (1) original Kirchenbuch image — inaccessible as browse-only microfilm; no different naming outcome is expected given index consistency confirmed by four sibling corroborations; (2) the couple's marriage record — inaccessible via indexed search and original browse not performed, but would corroborate the couple's union rather than alter Magdalena's parentage; (3) external repositories (Landesarchiv, Matricula) — out-of-session, no reason to anticipate contradicting evidence. Liechtenstein civil registration began 1878 (wiki confirmed), so no civil birth record exists for 1743. The baptismal register is the decisive record and was found.

hypotheses.claim: The 'Catharina Schedlerin' named as mother in Magdalena's 1743 christening (src_001) and the 'Catharina Gosnerin' named in the four sibling christenings (src_002–005) are the same woman, recorded under two conventions of the Triesen Catholic register: 'Schedlerin' (feminized husband's surname) versus 'Gosnerin' (feminized maiden surname).
hypotheses.notes: Working hypothesis accepted by GPS mentor (ev_001). The 'Schedlerin' form appears once in fifteen years of records from the same batch (C96026-1); all other four records use 'Gosnerin'. This is consistent with the documented regional naming convention in 18th-century Liechtenstein Catholic registers. See also h_002 for the competing hypothesis.

hypotheses.claim: Joannes Schedler had two different wives named Catharina in close succession: a first wife (Catharina Schedlerin) who died between 1741 and 1743, and a second wife (Catharina Gosnerin) who appears in the 1751–1756 records. Magdalena's 1743 christening records the first wife's surname.
hypotheses.ruled_out_reason: No death or remarriage record supports this reading. The 'Schedlerin' form appears in only one entry (Magdalena, 1743) among five entries spanning 1741–1756, all from the same register batch. A two-wife sequence would require a death between 1741 and 1743 and an almost-immediate remarriage to a second Catharina with no break in the parenting sequence — no evidence supports this. The Schedlerin/Gosnerin alternation is fully explained by the documented regional naming convention (feminized husband-surname vs. maiden-surname forms). Competing hypothesis h_001 is the preferred read.
hypotheses.notes: Competitor to h_001. Ruled out on methodological grounds (naming convention explains the variance; two-wife scenario requires unsupported events). Identified for structural evaluation by GPS mentor ev_001 (2026-09-23).

proof_summaries.narrative_markdown:
## Proof Summary: Parentage of Magdalena Schedler, christened 12 June 1743, Triesen, Liechtenstein

### Conclusion

The evidence strongly suggests that Magdalena, christened 12 June 1743 in Triesen, Liechtenstein, was a daughter of Joannes Schedler and Catharina Gosnerin. This conclusion rests on a derivative index record of her christening and four derivative index records of siblings christened in the same Triesen Catholic parish between 1741 and 1756, all of which name the same parental couple. The tier is **probable** because all five sources are derivative (FamilySearch index entries based on FHL microfilm of the original Triesen Kirchenbuch); the original register image was documented as inaccessible (browse-only microfilm) during this research session and was not directly examined.

### Direct Evidence

A FamilySearch index entry for the christening of Magdalena Schedler on 12 June 1743 in Triesen, Liechtenstein unambiguously names her father as Joannes Schedler and her mother as Catharina Schedlerin.[^1] This entry is an original contemporaneous parish registration act, but it is accessible only through a derivative index (FamilySearch collection 1708589, citing FHL microfilm of the Triesen Kirchenbuch); the underlying register image was not examined in this session.

The christening date and place are recorded in primary information supplied by the officiating parish priest — a witness to the ceremony — and carry `information_quality: primary`, `informant: parish priest`, `informant_proximity: witness`, `record_basis: stated`. The parentage statements are primary information supplied by the presenting parents — household members with firsthand knowledge of the child's parentage — and similarly carry `information_quality: primary`, `record_basis: stated`.

### The Schedlerin / Gosnerin Naming Variation

In the direct christening record (src_001), the mother appears as "Catharina Schedlerin" rather than "Catharina Gosnerin." This is not a conflict. Schedlerin is the feminine/declensional form of the husband's surname Schedler, reflecting a documented 18th-century Catholic parish-register practice in Liechtenstein whereby a married woman could be recorded either under her own maiden surname (feminized with the -in suffix) or under her husband's surname (also feminized with the -in suffix). Both forms designate the same woman: the assertion for the mother's name (a_008) documents this convention explicitly in its `informant_bias_notes`. All four sibling records (src_002–005) name the same mother as "Catharina Gosnerin" — the maiden-surname form — consistent with the tree person KZS8-RS7. The internal consistency across five registration events from the same register, spanning fifteen years, resolves any superficial ambiguity: "Catharina Schedlerin" in src_001 and "Catharina Gosnerin" in src_002–005 refer to one person.

### FAN Corroboration from Sibling Christenings

Four additional christening records from the same Triesen Catholic parish register (FamilySearch batch C96026-1) independently corroborate the parental couple:

- **Antonius Schedler**, christened 7 December 1741, Triesen: father Joannes Schedler, mother Catharina Gosnerin.[^2]
- **Josephus Schedler**, christened 12 November 1751, Triesen: father Joannes Schedler, mother Catharina Gosnerin.[^3]
- **Rosa Schedler**, christened 19 January 1754, Triesen: father Joannes Schedler, mother Catharina Gosnerin.[^4]
- **Antonius Schedler** (second child of that name, reflecting the common Catholic practice of reusing a saint's name after infant death), christened 12 June 1756, Triesen: father Joannes Schedler, mother Catharina Gosnerin.[^5]

Each of these five christening records was created at a separate ceremony on a different date with different presenting parents serving as informants at each distinct occasion. Although all five derive from the same institutional source (the Triesen Kirchenbuch), each is an independent registration event. The consistent identification of Joannes Schedler and Catharina Gosnerin (or Schedlerin) as parents across five separate acts of registration — spanning fifteen years from 1741 to 1756 — strongly supports the identity of Magdalena's parents.

### Source Classification and Research Scope

All five sources are **derivative** (FamilySearch database index entries, published 7 February 2020, derived from FHL microfilm of the Triesen Kirchenbuch): src_001, src_002, src_003, src_004, and src_005.[^1][^2][^3][^4][^5] The original parish register image (Triesen Kirchenbuch, FHL microfilm) was documented as browse-only and inaccessible during this research session (pli_002, skipped as inaccessible); it was not directly examined. The derivative character of all five sources, and the inability to verify the entries against the original register image, limits the conclusion to the probable tier rather than proved. All five records carry primary information for the parentage relationships, because in each case the presenting parents — the parties with firsthand knowledge of the child's parentage — supplied that information at the time of the registration event.

FamilySearch collection 1708589 is the only indexed online repository for Triesen Catholic christening records covering the 1743 period, and it was searched fully. Civil registration in Liechtenstein began in 1878 and family registers in 1789 — neither covers a 1743 christening event. The Triesen Kirchenbuch is therefore the decisive record type for this jurisdiction and period. No conflicting evidence was found in any of the five records or in any other source consulted.

### Assessment

No conflicts exist in this project. The only limitation is that the sources are derivative rather than original: no source examined is the original Kirchenbuch image itself. A future session in which a researcher can access the browse-only FHL microfilm image of the Triesen Kirchenbuch and directly examine the 1743 entry would provide the original-source confirmation needed to elevate this conclusion to **proved**. Until that image is examined, the conclusion rests at **probable**: the preponderance of evidence strongly supports the identification of Joannes Schedler and Catharina Gosnerin as Magdalena's parents, with no contradicting evidence and no unresolved conflicts.

localities.guide_markdown:
# Locality Guide: Triesen, Liechtenstein — 1743

## Jurisdictional Context

Triesen is a municipality in the Principality of Liechtenstein, a microstate bordered by Switzerland (west/south) and Austria (east). In 1743 Liechtenstein was a sovereign principality within the Holy Roman Empire and had been so since 1719. Records are organized at the municipality level. Triesen has existed as a municipality since at least 1208. There are no boundary splits within the target period that affect where records are held. The official language is German; Catholic church records of this era are in Latin.

Liechtenstein's entire territory belongs to the Roman Catholic Diocese of Chur (Switzerland), which was the ecclesiastical jurisdiction that governed parish record-keeping in 1743.

## Record Landscape for 1743

### 1. Catholic Parish (Church) Records — PRIMARY SOURCE

**Triesen Kirchenbuch (Parish Register), 1638–1916**
- FamilySearch Catalog: [#115845](https://www.familysearch.org/en/search/catalog/115845)
- Record types: Baptisms, marriages, deaths/burials, confirmations, family registers
- Baptismal entries record: date/place of baptism, child's name, parents' names, godparents' names
- Status: **Microfilmed; being digitized** — may be available as browse-only images at a FamilySearch Center or online
- Language: **Latin** (Catholic ecclesiastical practice, 1743)
- This is the definitive primary source for a christening on 12 June 1743

### 2. FamilySearch Indexed Collection — PARTIAL/INCOMPLETE

**[Liechtenstein, Births and Baptisms, 1650–1875](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/1708589)** (Collection ID: 1708589)
- 34,173 indexed records; 102,269 persons in index; 34,173 images
- Date range covers 1743
- **IMPORTANT CAVEATS**: This is a Legacy Collection — no new records will be added, no corrections made. The wiki warns the Triesen portion is very sparse; a negative search result here does not confirm absence. Population coverage before 1800 is only ~50%. Always verify any finding against the original parish image.
- Also available (as index) at: [Ancestry.com](https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/9913) ($), [MyHeritage](http://www.myheritage.com/research/collection-30204/liechtenstein-births-baptisms-1650-1875) ($), [FindMyPast](https://search.findmypast.com/search-world-Records/liechtenstein-births-and-baptisms-1650-1875) ($)

### 3. Civil Registration — NOT APPLICABLE for 1743
- Civil registration of births begins in Triesen in 1878; family registers (Familienbücher) begin 1789
- Neither covers a 1743 christening

### 4. Diocesan Archive Transcripts — NOT APPLICABLE for 1743
- Parish register transcripts (Kirchenbuchduplikate) for Liechtenstein are held in the Diocesan Archives, Chur, Switzerland, but begin as early as 1784 — they do not cover 1743

### 5. Familienbuch (Compiled Family Register)
- Triesen Standsamt, 1794–1956 (FamilySearch catalog [#103425](https://www.familysearch.org/en/search/catalog/103425))
- May retrospectively list earlier family members but is a derivative/compiled source; confirm any entry against the original 1743 baptismal register

## Search Strategy

1. **Search the FamilySearch indexed collection 1708589 first** — quick and free. Search for: child Magdalena Schedler, father Joannes/Johannes Schedler, mother Catharina, place Triesen, date range 1743.
2. **If not found in the index, browse the Triesen Kirchenbuch images** (catalog #115845). The register covers 1638 forward; locate the 1743 baptismal pages and read page-by-page for the 12 June 1743 entry. Records are in Latin/Kurrent script.
3. **If not found in Triesen, search neighboring parishes**: Balzers (south), Triesenberg (east), Vaduz (north). Families near parish borders sometimes appear in adjacent registers.
4. **Cross-border search**: Triesen is near the Swiss border — if the family had connections across the border, Swiss parish records (Canton St. Gallen, Diocese of Chur) may be relevant.

## Language and Script
- Church records in Latin; civil documents in German
- Handwriting: Kurrent script (Gothic German cursive)
- Resources: [German Genealogical Word List](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/German_Genealogical_Word_List), [Latin Genealogical Word List](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Latin_Genealogical_Word_List), [German Handwriting guide](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Germany_Handwriting)

## Repositories
- **FamilySearch** (online): Collection 1708589; catalog items for microfilmed registers
- **Liechtenstein Civil Registry**: St. Florinsgasse 3, 9490 Vaduz, Liechtenstein (post-1878 records)
- **Diocesan Archives, Chur, Switzerland**: Transcripts from 1784 onward
- **Local parish archive, Triesen**: Original register may be consulted in person
